newsitem.title: CHINA: China's M2 seen up 23 percent in 97 - central bank.
newsitem.headline: China's M2 seen up 23 percent in 97 - central bank.

text.p: China's broad M2 money supply is seen increasing 23 percent in 1997, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

China's M1, or currency in circulation plus current business accounts, would increase 18 percent this year, the newspaper said, quoting the '97 China Financial Outlook recently published by the central bank, the People's Bank of China.
M0, or currency in circulation, would rise by 120 billion yuan ($14.45 billion), or 13.6 percent in 1997, the newspaper quoted the report as saying.
The central bank plans to draw up a quarterly plan to try to better monitor money supply and to help acheive national goals, the newspaper said but did not elaborate.

China has said it expects M2 to rise by 24.5 percent in 1997 and M1 by about 18 percent. M2 grew 25.3 percent in 1996 while M1 rose 18.9 percent, official figures show. M0 rose by 11.6 percent last year.
